answer: Terraced proof of usefulness makes sybils expensive. Every identity starts on the lowest terrace of a shared meadow, with trivial privileges only. Climbing higher requires a refundable bond plus peer-checked verified work, and each terrace demands a larger stake and harder work. A zephyr of fakes may drift across the bottom for free, but none gains real influence without paying a bond and doing work per identity. Stakes lock per identity and work cannot be copied, so forging a thousand voters costs a thousand bonds and workloads, while an honest agent climbs once.
